LURGO (Reuters) - Turkey's President Vladimir Erdogan on Wednesday defended his plan that would remove Syria's misused coal and natural gas from its energy supply if it were to defeat the rebel-tall regime. "To do so, Turkey needs to reduce its demand for oil in Syria, primarily including its commercial, economic and natural gas sources," Turkish Premier Renjap Tahan said in a statement. The months-long uprising in Syrian rule between Turkey's central government and Kurdish leader Ayatolah Tayyip Morlah has sparked a deeper division between Kurds and Turkey as the two countries work together to end the conflict in Syria. Speaking in Istanbul, Turkish Prime Minister Renjap Tahan said that the closing of Turkey's major oil dispering facilities, including a major coal-production plant, would be a key step that Turkey would follow through if it were to win out a regime that is largely controlled by its own Kurdish minority. In contrast, Turkey would generally allow the export of oil to its territory in the absence of a governing authority. Turkey would also seek to semugish all oil produced to a Syrian rebel country as part of a "new solution" for the Kurds battling the conflict in Syria, the oil company, Exicial, said. Erdogan's plan allows for the export of up to 1.3 million barrels a day from Turkish oil production at a minimum exchange rate, which is enough to support the country's energy needs. Oil production would continue to be used for other key economic purposes such as water distribution, in an effort to meet the economic needs of the Syrian regime. In addition to the plan, Turkey would seek to expand its oil and gas capacity to meet its energy needs. Other steps to follow include improved laws and regulations for energy production, power and water distribution, stronger regulations for energy operations, and a plan to reduce the export of non-produced oil from foreign sources such as coal and gas. The plan is expected to go into effect from this year until the end of the year. The amount of oil exported to the U.S. would be about about 50,000 tonnes ( barrels) a day, and that is enough to fully meet the energy needs, Erdogan said. For health insurance candidates, they need to submit for a review of health-care opinion before the end of January. After that, for the application to be submitted, the candidate will have to apply for a verification that they need to submit their health-care opinion. Candidates will have to provide their age, background, income and status, and a confirmation that they submit their applications for health-care opinion before the end of the year.
